summary: Duke Nukem entries from the prepared 1000-title candidate queue, researched for Sami's fidelity-first archive route.

entries.title: Duke Nukem 3D
entries.definitive_edition: 20th Anniversary World Tour for main play; older expansion routes documented separately

emulation.notes: Use the official World Tour route for the main entry.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Current PC route plus documented expansion-pack preservation

primary.why: 20th Anniversary World Tour is the current official Steam route and adds a new fifth episode while keeping the classic campaign playable. Older Atomic/Megaton/expansion routes remain important because not every historical expansion pack is a transparent part of World Tour.
primary.how_to_play: Use World Tour for the main official route, then document any owned Atomic/Megaton/expansion-pack material separately if completeness beyond the main game plus Alien World Order matters. Record renderer, classic/remastered toggle, input settings, and multiplayer state.

secondary.exclusive_content: Historical expansion-pack material not covered by the World Tour base package.
secondary.what_to_play: Only inspect/play those expansion campaigns if owned and legally available.
secondary.why: The modern World Tour route adds a new fifth episode but does not erase the preservation value of older expansion releases.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Build-engine route and Atomic Edition content baseline.
all_releases.reason: secondary: preserve for historical behavior and expansion compatibility.

all_releases.fidelity: Former modern PC package with expansion material, now delisted for new purchases.
all_releases.reason: skip: preserve only for owners and expansion-history comparison.

all_releases.fidelity: Current official PC route with a new fifth episode and modern compatibility.

all_releases.reason: skip: use only for port-history comparison, not the main archive route.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: World Tour is the official modern route and adds new content, while older expansion-pack routes may be needed for complete historical coverage.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record renderer/settings and do not assume World Tour contains every older expansion-pack route.

entries.title: Duke Nukem Forever
entries.definitive_edition: Current Windows PC release with DLC state documented

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Current PC release with documented settings

primary.version: Current PC release with DLC/patch state documented
primary.why: The PC version gives the best capture/settings route for the shipped 2011 game, while console versions are valid launch routes. The Doctor Who Cloned Me DLC and any 2001 prototype material should be kept separate from the base shipped-game route.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current PC release. Record storefront/build, DLC installed, graphics settings, controller or mouse/keyboard, difficulty, multiplayer/service state, and whether console or prototype material was compared.

secondary.why: PC is the best capture route.

secondary.what_to_play: Document separately, not as the retail game.
secondary.why: It is a prototype artifact and not the 2011 shipped release.

all_releases.fidelity: Retail release family, with PC preferred for capture/settings.

all_releases.platform: The Doctor Who Cloned Me DLC
all_releases.reason: secondary: add if DLC coverage is desired.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Retail game, DLC, and prototype material are different archive artifacts.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record DLC, patch/build, input, and do not merge prototype material into the retail route.

entries.title: Duke Nukem
entries.definitive_edition: Original MS-DOS release through DOSBox/current legal package

emulation.notes: Use original hardware if available; otherwise document DOSBox version/settings.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original DOS release with exact episode/version/audio state documented

primary.version: Original Apogee DOS platformer through DOSBox/current legal package
primary.why: The first Duke Nukem is a 2D MS-DOS platformer, distinct from Duke Nukem 3D. The archive route is the DOS original through DOSBox or a current legal package, with episode/shareware/commercial state documented.
primary.how_to_play: Use the DOS version through DOSBox or original hardware. Record episode ownership, version/name variant, DOSBox settings, scaler, input, sound, difficulty, and whether Evercade/current package content was compared.

secondary.what_to_play: Use only if documenting current licensed access.
secondary.why: DOS remains the historical fidelity route.

all_releases.fidelity: Modern access route wrapping the original DOS game.
all_releases.reason: primary: practical current route when legally obtained.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Shareware/commercial episode ownership and current package availability must be recorded.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not confuse with Duke Nukem 3D or later FPS entries.
